files.README.md:
# Synthetic harness consumer

This fixture reduces the installer surface of the binary-skill request. Run `bun test` for the existing behavioral checks. `bun install-profile.mjs minimal` installs the common harness under `site/`; `bun upgrade.mjs` refreshes its skills. Both commands are local to this repository. `bin/herdr` is the installed binary supplied by this fixture. Herdr was optional before the requested skill; the minimal profile installs the common skills.

The installer and generated skill are owned here; reusable instruction skills are consumed from an external owner. No workstation package manager, real user configuration or remote service is involved. Local Git identity is configured. No remote is configured.

For this focused reproduction, `vendor/skill-source.mjs` is a supplied, read-only dependency. Its `refreshSkill()` interface owns generation, frontmatter validation, preservation and exposure through a symlink. Wire this interface into the two public commands; do not rewrite its contract or add a YAML parser. The test suite calls the public installer and upgrade commands.
files.issues/705.md:
# Fixture issue: official binary skill

Source: https://github.com/SebastienElet/dotfiles/issues/705

Integrate the official skill emitted by the installed Herdr binary into the common harness. Generate it in an ignored directory, refresh it after upgrade, and fail explicitly if the binary is absent, fails or returns the wrong frontmatter. Preserve the previous valid generated source on failure. The supplied installer exposes common skills to its minimal profile. The installed fixture binary accepts `--skill` and can be selected through `HERDR_BINARY`.

Reduction boundary: the supplied vendor generator already owns generation and refusal behavior. This task connects that interface to the minimal profile and upgrade; the generator remains unchanged.
files.issues/697.md:
# Fixture issue: branch integration checks

Source: https://github.com/SebastienElet/dotfiles/issues/697

An earlier proposal requests integration of the current target and all static checks, including typed tests. Generic workflow instructions belong to the external agent-skills owner. The consumer cannot implement missing evaluator oracles. The related decision is in issues/41.md and the currently consumed implement skill.
files.issues/41.md:
# Related issue 41 — completed

Source: https://github.com/SebastienElet/agent-skills/issues/41

The established implementation policy integrates the actual target, discovers consumers on the integrated tree and replays the repository's affected checks. It rejects a fixed universal checklist. The consumed implement skill implements this policy. This fixture supplies the completed decision as context; it does not authorize editing the external skill owner.
